_comment: Invrisil 8c Task C1 (issue #12) -- ~20x14 mercantile alleys, the stealth playground (locked shape: bent routes, stacked crates, 2-3 SNEAKABLE trigger_radius footpad placements). biome invrisil_alley (FIX WAVE: same wang paving floor as the boulevard per direction.md's 'same stone, meaner hour', but its OWN blocked+skirt -- the darker textured masonry band picks.md sec.2 flagged for alley walls -- after the controller's windowed read caught the shared-street version rendering as corridors floating on void; see biomes.json's invrisil_alley _comment). Sparse sconce lantern pools on wall cells (decor below) + the night mood card carry the 'lantern maze' read -- direction doc open-question 4's own fence-less fallback. The open path is a bent L: a west corridor (y6-7) -> a north-south connector (x8-10) -> an east corridor (y11-12) to the parlor door, matching the design doc's 'bent routes' literally, not just in flavor -- footpads sit IN the turn and just past it. Crate/barrel decor dresses the corridor's blocked-adjacent cells (the 'CLIMBABLE flavor, not literal climbing' note -- stacked goods, not scatter).

decor._comment: FIX WAVE lantern pools (direction.md alleys card: 'sparse fence-lantern anchors, wider gaps between pools than the boulevard's serviced rhythm'). Reuses the existing `sconce` sprite (the inn's own wall lamp -- zero new assets, the direction doc's own 'consider owned/wired art instead of the speculative sewer lantern pick' note) on wall cells adjacent to the corridors. Four pools over three corridor legs vs the boulevard's eight -- the sparser rhythm IS the card. Non-flicker per the direction card's Invrisil-wide rule (serviced city lamps; flicker reads poor).

entities._comment: Round-trip pair with boulevard_to_alleys (invrisil_boulevard cell 26,8). Landing (25,8) on the boulevard side is the open mid-street cell immediately west of that door.
Round-trip pair with parlor_to_alleys (brothers_parlor cell 0,4). Landing (1,4) on the parlor side is the open interior cell immediately east of that door.
entities.display_name: A Plain Door, Better Locks Than It Looks

entities._comment: Invrisil 8c Task C1 -- the street fixer, 'Cups' (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-invrisil-design.md sec.2/sec.4: 'sells rumors by the CUP -- tea-house pricing bit'). FULL conversation graph wired now (data/dialogue/invrisil_fixer.json) -- unlike Wilovan/Coyle, none of her effects reference a quest id or a start_combat entity C1 doesn't own (gold/accomplishment only), so the rumor-vending hub + the TALK-path testimony chain's *shape* are safe to ship now; the testimony options stay naturally hidden (requires took_brothers_job/fixer_will_testify, both absent==0) until Task C3 lands the quest that banks them -- a forward reference, same convention as C2's Wilovan combatant record. Sprite: reused `citizen_f` rig tinted muted teal-grey (a shawl-and-tea-tray read), zero new generation.
entities.observe: A tea-tray harness worn shiny at the left shoulder — she pours right-handed and listens left-eared. The cups are chipped. The ears are not.
entities.friendly_line: She pours you a cup without being asked. "On the house," she says, "which is the only kind of trade I ever regret."

dialogue.speaker: Cups
dialogue.text: Tea's free. Rumor's a gold the cup.

entities._comment: LOCKED interface (8c plan) -- `alley_footpads_a`, one of 2-3 sneakable trigger_radius encounters (the K2 payoff: traced _check_trigger_radius before placing -- `sneaking` skips the ambush entirely and instead banks sneaked_past_danger, silently, per that function's own doc comment; walking it WITHOUT sneaking fires start_combat for real). Arena `mercantile_alley`, roster `footpad_lookout`/`footpad_bruiser` (lane beta/C2's combat data, tuned LOW-lethality by design so a failed sneak never walls the player). Sits inside the vertical connector (the bent route's turn), the corridor's narrowest point.
entities.observe: Two figures loitering with the specific stillness of people about to stop pretending they're not waiting for you.

entities._comment: LOCKED interface -- `alley_footpads_b`, the pair's second placement (east corridor, toward the parlor door). Chebyshev distance from alley_footpads_a's own radius-2 zone is 5 (dx5/dy3) -- deliberately non-overlapping, so a canonical script can sneak past BOTH independently without _check_trigger_radius's single-fire-per-move loop masking one behind the other.
entities.observe: The second pair, closer to the counting-house door — same trick, same stillness, better light to see it by.

entities._comment: Invrisil 8c Task C3 (issue #13) -- the STEALTH/SKILL path's own beat: 'the [Observe] true-books + keen-eye hidden-safe beat' (spec sec.3), through the propped yard-side door Cups' rumor already named (invrisil_fixer.json's rumor_counting_house: 'the clerk with the inky cuffs... props it with a cheese wedge'). Mirrors the shield-spider `nest_ledge`/pantry-doorframe SKILL-prop shape EXACTLY: `requires_skill: observe` (the [Appraise Foe] Tactician grant -- NOTE the 2026-07-07 canon rename [Observe]->[Appraise Foe], id `observe` unchanged; the spec/plan's own prose still says '[Observe]', which now reads STALE against the shipped skill catalog -- toast copy below uses the CURRENT display name, not the plan's) + `on_skill_use` banks `lifted_true_ledger` deterministically (zero rng), matching the number/date accusation.json's own accusation-node option quotes verbatim (forty gold, dated the night before). The hidden-safe beat is folded into the SAME single reveal rather than a second prop -- the ledger drawer's own false back is where the safe sits (an honest scope collapse for a single-cell abstraction of 'the counting-house', which this map doesn't model as a separate interior; flagged for controller review). PLACEMENT FIX (this lane's own regression catch, same class as hired_blades' own note below): originally (17,11) sat DIRECTLY on invrisil_walkthrough's own pinned sneak-positive route (right 8 from (10,11) to (18,11), walked BOTH directions including the epilogue) -- entity occupancy silently blocked that shipped C1 canonical. Relocated to (16,12), east corridor floor between alley_footpads_b (14,12) and the parlor door (19,12) -- a cell that script's own asserted route never steps on (it drops straight from (18,11) to (18,12), never touching x15-17 on row 12). Chebyshev distance 2 from alley_footpads_b's own trigger_radius-2 zone is irrelevant here (my own canonical script reaches this prop via `teleport` + a stationary `interact`, never a `move` step near it, and `_check_trigger_radius` only ever runs from `move_player`). Sprite `dusty_scroll` reused (the retired [Light]-study prop, thematically apt for 'something to read with a skill' -- the doorframe-runes precedent), zero new generation. GH#68 (quest-stage rework) GATE ADDED: the real evidence now needs `assessed_guard_pattern` banked first (`counting_house_watch`, this map's own new prop, below) -- reuses the on_skill_use `variants` seam verbatim (the cellar_door precedent, wi_game.gd's `_resolve_skill_use_effect`), no new sim code. Base effect fires on an [Appraise Foe] attempt made before the guard pattern is known (bank a real, harmless, disclosed flavor counter -- `noticed_the_clean_ledger` -- never the true ledger); the variant overrides both `accomplishment` and `toast` once `assessed_guard_pattern` is already banked. `locked_toast` (skill UNKNOWN case) is untouched.
entities.skill_hint_toast: The clean ledger is the tell. Sizing up what is really here takes a practiced read.

on_skill_use.toast: The desk's own ledger reads clean -- too clean, the kind of clean a man pays for. Whatever's real is hidden better than this. You'll want to know how this place is watched before you go digging further.

variants.toast: [Appraise Foe] — Now you know the gap in the watch, the true ledger comes easy: tucked behind a false-backed drawer no honest desk needs. Forty gold to a 'removal man,' dated the night before Coyle's own theft: his hand, his numbers, his mistake. The drawer's second catch gives up a shallow hidden safe behind it, empty now but scored where something heavier than coin sat until recently.

entities.locked_toast: The desk's own ledger reads clean, which is exactly the kind of clean a man pays for. You don't have the eye to find the real one. Not yet.

entities._comment: GH#68 (Invrisil quest-stage rework): the SKILL path's Stage 2 gate -- the counting-house's guard rotation, watched from a shadowed nook before ever trying the desk itself. Ungated [Appraise Foe] use (single interaction -- the guard-pattern/ledger PAIR is the 'two interactions, two locations' the stage map calls for; this prop itself needs no prerequisite). Sprite `dusty_scroll` reused (same 'something to read with a skill' idiom as the ledger it gates), tint distinguishes it from the ledger's own sprite use. Cell (15,12): free floor, adjacent to counting_house_ledger (16,12) and alley_footpads_b (14,12) -- off invrisil_walkthrough's own pinned route (that script never steps on (15,12), only (18,11)/(18,12) on this stretch), reached via teleport by the SKILL canonical (never a walked `move` step near footpads_b's trigger_radius).
entities.skill_hint_toast: Two men keep the counting-house door. Sizing up their rhythm takes a practiced read.

on_skill_use.toast: [Appraise Foe] — Two men on the counting-house door, and they're sloppier than they think: the same slow circuit, the same gap while both backs are turned, near enough on the bell to set a watch by. Time it right and the desk inside is yours for a minute, maybe two.

entities.locked_toast: Two men on the door, pacing something. You don't have the eye to time it yet.

entities._comment: GH#68 (Invrisil quest-stage rework): the FIGHT path's Stage 2 tailing chain, second leg (pairs with `coyle_runner_trail`, invrisil_boulevard). Plain on_interact_accomplishment, no skill gate (a fighter-built PC must never need [Appraise Foe] to reach a fight). Banks the counter invrisil_wilovan.json's `fists_door` come-along ask gates on. Cell (19,11): free floor, off invrisil_walkthrough's own pinned route (that script's sneak leg touches (18,11)/(18,12), never (19,11)) and off both footpad trigger_radius zones. FIGHT-path-only, reached via teleport in near_invrisil_fight/invrisil_disagreement_fight -- never walked by the shared invrisil_walkthrough canonical.
entities.observe: The runner's trail ends at a side door with fresh boot-scuff on the sill and burgundy-and-brass livery moving past the gap in the shutters. Coyle's crew, and no mistaking the building now.
entities.toast: The runner ducks inside, and you finally see the whole of it: crates stacked to the rafters, more of Coyle's livery than a legitimate warehouse ever needs. Wherever the come-along ends, it ends here.

entities._comment: Invrisil 8c Task C3 (issue #13) -- `hired_blades`, the LOCKED interface id (plan's lane map: arena `merchant_warehouse`, on_victory banking the confrontation flag) for the quest's FIGHT path: Coyle's warehouse crew. Interact-only (no trigger_radius), the crate/cisterns/rift_vermin_leak FIGHT-leg precedent -- 'the fight lives on its own map, reached by the player's own feet', no dialogue-side start_combat wiring required (though invrisil_merchant_prince.json's accusation node ALSO offers a second, reactive entry into this SAME entity id via its '(Draw steel.)' option -- both routes converge on one start_combat(id) call, per wi_game.gd's own single-choke-point design). `allies: ["wilovan"]` + `ally_requires: {wilovan_will_fight: 1}` is the come-along gate, banked ONLY by data/dialogue/invrisil_wilovan.json's `fists_door` ask (no teleporting allies, the riverfarm_hunter/relc_descent precedent) -- matches combatants.json's own wilovan record + sim_combat_batch.gd's `hired_blades_w10_wilovan`/`hired_blades_w10_solo` harness cells (gated 0.6-0.8 with the ally, measured-only solo). `on_victory: forced_confession` is the accomplishment invrisil_merchant_prince.json's hub/cornered nodes both key on -- kept as the DRAFT dialogue's literal wired string (the plan's own lane-map prose paraphrases this 'forced_the_confession'; using the draft's exact string keeps data and dialogue internally consistent, flagged for controller review same as the wilovan file's own note). PLACEMENT FIX (this lane's own regression catch): originally placed at (6,7) in the west corridor, which sits DIRECTLY on invrisil_walkthrough's own pinned sneak-negative route (right 6 from (1,7) to (7,7)) -- entity occupancy blocks movement, so that placement silently broke the shipped C1 canonical (caught by re-running it, not by test_content, which has no route-collision check). Relocated to (17,12), east corridor, south of the new counting_house_ledger prop (17,11) and Chebyshev distance 3 from alley_footpads_b (14,12) -- outside its trigger_radius-2 zone -- and NOT on any cell invrisil_walkthrough's script asserts or steps through (it drops straight from (18,11) to (18,12) without ever touching x15-17 on row 12). Sprite `hired_blade` (C2's owned PixelLab rig) -- ANCHOR RULE machine-playtest verification still owed per combatants.json's own comment (a windowed check, out of this headless lane's verification scope; flagged for the controller).
entities.observe: Three men in burgundy-and-brass doublets, clubs and knives held like men who've used them before. Merchant-livery, not Watch steel — Coyle's, all the way down to the stitching.

entities.skill_hint_toast: A snag-line at ankle height, tied crate to drainpipe. Old footpad work, the kind meant to trip a running mark. Worth clearing.
entities.locked_toast: A taut line crosses the alley at ankle height, tied off crate to drainpipe. It's clearly meant to trip someone. You can't see how to clear it safely.

on_skill_use.toast: You unhook the line and coil it loose. A couple of coins sit tucked in the crate it was tied to, payment nobody came back to collect.

entities.skill_hint_toast: A stack of crates wedged just wrong, top-heavy and set to come down on whoever pulls from the bottom. Old footpad mischief.
entities.locked_toast: The crate stack looks ordinary until you notice the angle: top-heavy, wedged to fall. Pulling from the bottom feels like a very bad idea.

on_skill_use.toast: You brace the stack and ease the wedge free by hand. Behind the bottom crate: a couple of coins someone forgot to collect.
